note: First election of the rural district council (four district electoral divisions, two councillors each), polled 6 April 1899. At the first meeting Maynard Sinton and William Adams were co-opted and three additional councillors chosen (Banbridge Chronicle, 19 April 1899, p. 3); they are not filed. Returned unopposed. Five were nominated (William Andrews, John Blacker, Thomas Collen, William John M'Intyre and Archibald Haire: Northern Whig, 18 March 1899, p. 7). No poll is reported for Mullahead, and the Banbridge Chronicle's list of the new council names Hare and Collen; the withdrawals were not found. Blacker and M'Intyre were among those put forward as additional councillors at the first meeting.
